title: Create files and directories
summary: Build and verify a clearly named directory tree with mkdir, mkdir -p, touch, and a recursive listing.

content.objective: Create a precise, clearly named directory tree with mkdir and mkdir -p, create empty regular files with touch, and verify every path and type with a recursive listing.
content.instructions: Work only in the supplied build-zone and complete the tasks in order. Create field-notes, add its nested research/sources path, create the two requested empty files with clear names, and verify the finished tree. Use the exact relative paths requested and create no extra entries. If you make a naming mistake, reset rather than using commands from later lessons.

fixtures.content:
TARGET TREE
field-notes/
  README.txt
  research/
    sources/
      web-links.txt

tasks.title: Create the project directory
tasks.instructions: Use plain mkdir to create one directory named field-notes in the current build-zone. Before running the command, predict that the relative name will create a child of the current working directory.

tasks.title: Create the nested research path
tasks.instructions: In one command, use mkdir with its parent-creation option to create field-notes/research/sources. The field-notes directory already exists; research and sources do not.

tasks.title: Create two clearly named files
tasks.instructions: Use one touch command to create field-notes/README.txt and field-notes/research/sources/web-links.txt, in that order. Both names communicate purpose, and both parent directories now exist.

tasks.title: Verify the complete tree
tasks.instructions: Run ls -R field-notes to list this small tree recursively. Use the section headings and names to verify that README.txt is directly in field-notes and web-links.txt is under research/sources. Leave the finished structure unchanged.

params.value:
TARGET TREE
field-notes/
  README.txt
  research/
    sources/
      web-links.txt

hints.text: Use the command whose name means make directory. Give it one clear relative name so the new directory becomes a child of the cwd.
The command is mkdir, and the required child name is field-notes. Do not add an option for this first single directory.
Plain mkdir needs the immediate parent to exist. Add mkdir's option for creating missing parent components, then provide the complete nested path.
Use -p with mkdir. Resolve field-notes/research/sources from left to right; field-notes exists, while the last two components need creation.
Use the command that creates a missing empty file. It accepts more than one file path, but every parent directory must already exist.
Use touch followed first by the README path directly under field-notes and then by the web-links path under research/sources. Preserve capitalization and the hyphen.
Use the familiar listing command with its recursive option and field-notes as the path. Compare every heading and name with the target tree.
The recursive option is uppercase -R. A correct listing shows README.txt and research, then sources below research, then web-links.txt below sources.

tutor.goalSummary: Student plans relative paths, creates one directory with mkdir, creates missing nested parents with mkdir -p, creates two precisely named empty files with touch, and verifies the resulting types and nesting instead of assuming success.
misconceptions: mkdir creates directories, while touch creates the empty regular files required in this lesson.
Plain mkdir requires the immediate parent to exist; mkdir -p creates missing parent components but also reproduces any mistyped component.
touch does not create missing parent directories, write the filename as content, or normally erase an existing file.
Relative creation paths begin at the current working directory, so the student should predict the complete location before running a command.
Linux names are case-sensitive; README.txt and readme.txt are different paths.
A successful silent command is not a substitute for verifying the complete resulting tree.
constraints: Keep coaching within mkdir, mkdir -p, touch, clear naming, relative-path reasoning, and verification with ls -R.
Do not suggest rm, rmdir, mv, cp, redirection, editors, shell loops, command chaining, or absolute creation paths.
Give each task's hints in level order; ask the student to predict the resulting path or listing before revealing the exact command at level 3.
Do not provide all four commands as one pasteable sequence or complete later tasks for the student.
Require exact capitalization, hyphenation, and nesting; do not accept extra or vaguely named entries as craftsmanship.
If the student creates an incorrect entry, direct them to reset rather than teaching removal or renaming ahead of sequence.
Keep all work under workspace/build-zone and remind the student that fixture directories are writable mode 0755 for safe materialization and creation.
After completion, ask why -p was needed, why touch came after directory creation, and what evidence in ls -R established the nesting.
